mistakes.title: Missing decoupling capacitor
mistakes.explanation: U1 has a power pin on net 'VCC', but no bypass/decoupling capacitor connects that net to a recognized ground return. Without local decoupling, supply transients from switching current can couple into the IC and cause glitches, resets, or radiated noise.
mistakes.fix_suggestion: Add a decoupling capacitor (typically 100nF, or per the datasheet) from VCC to the nearest ground return, placed within a few mm of U1's power pin.

mistakes.title: Via in SMD pad
mistakes.explanation: Via found in SMD pad 2 of R4. During reflow soldering, solder can wick down into the via, resulting in insufficient solder on the pad and unreliable connections.
mistakes.fix_suggestion: Move the via outside the pad area, or specify via-in-pad with filled and capped vias in the manufacturing notes. Via-in-pad increases cost but is acceptable when properly filled.

mistakes.title: Acute angle in trace (acid trap)
mistakes.explanation: Trace on NODE_B (F.Cu) has a 45° angle. Angles less than 90° can trap etchant during PCB manufacturing, causing over-etching at the vertex. This can weaken the trace and cause reliability issues.
mistakes.fix_suggestion: Reroute the trace to use 45° or 90° angles instead. If the acute angle is unavoidable, add a teardrop at the junction to eliminate the sharp corner.
